title: You are the form of light
word: You are the form of light
hookLine: man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; know your origin (Asa M3, ang 441)
last: EGO AND THE NAME CAN'T SHARE ONE ROOM.

cards: Man too jot saroop hai. A short run of Punjabi that lands like a hand on the shoulder. Guru Amar Das has been talking to the mind like someone who keeps drifting off.
Here he stops calling it home for a moment and tells it what it is. Not a problem to fix. Not a list of failures.
A form of light. The line is in Raga Asa, on Ang four hundred forty-one of the Guru Granth Sahib, and it opens by speaking to the mind directly: man too. O mind, you.

teach.b: Here's the line, paraphrased: O my mind, you are the very form of light; recognize your own origin.
Jot is light, the same word Sikhs use for the light that passed from Guru to Guru. Saroop is form, likeness. Mool is root, origin, where something starts.
So the line holds a picture and an instruction. The picture: underneath the noise, you are light. The instruction: go find where it came from.
The hymn goes on, again paraphrased: O mind, the Lord is with you; through the Guru's teaching, enjoy that love.

teach.h: KNOW YOUR ROOT, KNOW YOUR LORD.
teach.b: Recognize your origin and you'll know your Lord, and understand dying and living. Notice the order. It doesn't say you are the Lord, so stop looking.
It says you are light, so look for the source of the light. Knowing yourself and knowing your Lord turn out to be one road. That fits the week behind us.
Guru Angad called the Guru a light in the darkness, warned that service can carry pride, and called ego an illness with its cure inside. Guru Amar Das said ego and the Name can't share a room.
And now, the reason the room is worth clearing: what lives there is light.
Some readers hear this line as the quiet center of all the warnings.
They aren't there because the mind is worthless. They're there because it's made of something precious, and keeps forgetting.

how: This line of Guru Amar Das from Raga Asa is often sung in kirtan and quoted in katha at the gurdwara; some Sikhs keep it as a reminder when they recite or reflect on their own.

games.q: what does “you are the form of light” mean?
o: the mind, underneath its noise, is made of light
a halo the Gurus wear in the old paintings
the lamp kept burning beside the scripture

games.q: the words inside the line: tap the pairs.

s: the line says the mind is worthless and must be fixed
it says the mind is the form of light, and asks it to recognize its origin.
the hymn ties knowing your origin to knowing your Lord
recognize your origin, it says, and you'll know your Lord.

games.q: the Guru tells the mind it is the form of light. what does the line ask it to do next?
o: stop searching; it already has everything.
recognize its origin, and so come to know its Lord.
keep the light hidden so no one sees it.
games.why: the line is a picture and an instruction: you are light; know your origin. knowing the root and knowing the Lord turn out to be one road.

practice: Let the words ride the breath: in, man too jot saroop hai; out, know your origin.

You don't have to work out what it means, only turn toward where your life came from and stay there gently, and if a harsh thought about yourself shows up, set it beside the line and let the line be louder.
If you pray, Waheguru can take the out-breath instead.

wordCard.voice: You are the form of light. Man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; recognize your origin. Today's word.

orig.note: the form of light: Guru Amar Das's words to the mind in Raga Asa.

carryVoice: Your line: you are light. That closes this week, from Guru Angad's few lines to Guru Amar Das's call to the mind. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Asa Mahala 3, Ang 441 (man too jot saroop hai, apna mool pachhan; O mind, the Lord is with you)
